results.1: (LG) The Knight of Cador. "One kingdom, one king, one people." Fought to preserve unity and believes victory obliges the crown to treat defeated subjects honorably.
results.2: (NG) The Compassionate Loyalist. "There was no glory in that war." Supported the crown but believes its conduct was frequently shameful.
results.3: (CG) The Southern Dissenter. "The ancient houses have ruled long enough." Sympathized with northern challenges to hereditary power, despite being raised in the south.
results.4: (LN) The Oathsworn Knight. "My father served the king. As did his father." Fought because fealty is the foundation of society, regardless of personal politics.
results.5: (N) The Conscripted Farmer. "The lord called the levy. What choice had I?" Fought because refusal meant punishment and his family depended upon his estate.
results.6: (CN) The Fortune-Seeking Sellsword. "The crown paid better." Joined the royal armies for coin, adventure, and the opportunity to earn a reputation.
results.7: (LE) The Blood-Proud Aristocrat. "A merchant is no noble, however rich." Supported the decree because northern exclusion would secure his family's political supremacy.
results.8: (NE) The Royal Profiteer. "Rebellion carries a price." Used royal authority to seize property and enrich himself through confiscations.
results.9: (CE) The Butcher. "Mercy only breeds another rebellion." Believes northern communities deserve collective punishment and advocates ruthless suppression.
results.10: (LG) The Reformist Royalist. "We won the kingdom back. Now we must make it worthy of keeping." Opposed the bloodline decree but fought to preserve unity.
results.11: (LN) The Traditionalist Steward. "Every man has his place, and every place its obligations." Believes hereditary hierarchy maintains peace and order, even if it restricts freedom.
results.12: (NG) The War-Weary Parent. "They say we won. My sons are still dead." Supported the king but now cares little for victory celebrations or political arguments.
